title: The Process Bottleneck
prompt: A critical workflow is taking 3x longer than it should. You've identified the bottleneck but fixing it requires buy-in from two other teams.

leftChoice.label: Push for cross-team alignment
leftChoice.outcomeText: After weeks of meetings, the fix is implemented. The process is now 60% faster. Worth it.

rightChoice.label: Build a workaround yourself
rightChoice.outcomeText: The workaround works but adds technical debt. The root cause remains.

title: The Vendor Negotiation
prompt: Your primary vendor just raised prices by 15%. You can renegotiate or switch to a cheaper alternative that's less reliable.

leftChoice.label: Renegotiate with current vendor
leftChoice.outcomeText: You negotiate them down to 8%. Not perfect but the relationship stays intact.

rightChoice.label: Switch to the cheaper vendor
rightChoice.outcomeText: The migration is painful. The new vendor has two outages in the first month. Finance loves the savings.

title: The SLA Breach
prompt: A key SLA was missed this week. The client is furious. The root cause was a vendor failure, not your team.

leftChoice.label: Own it and offer remediation
leftChoice.outcomeText: The client appreciates the accountability. The relationship is preserved.

rightChoice.label: Escalate the blame to the vendor
rightChoice.outcomeText: The client doesn't care whose fault it is. They just know you didn't fix it.

title: The Runbook Gap
prompt: A critical process has no documentation. It lives entirely in one person's head — and they just gave notice.

leftChoice.label: Drop everything and document it now
leftChoice.outcomeText: You spend a week shadowing them and building a comprehensive runbook. The team is relieved.

rightChoice.label: Hope the next hire figures it out
rightChoice.outcomeText: Three months later, a critical process fails. No one knows how to fix it. It takes two weeks to recover.

title: The Incident Response
prompt: A production incident is happening right now. You're the most senior person available. The on-call engineer is unreachable.

leftChoice.label: Take charge and coordinate the response
leftChoice.outcomeText: You lead the incident to resolution. It's stressful but your leadership is recognized company-wide.

rightChoice.label: Escalate up the chain and wait
rightChoice.outcomeText: The incident drags on while you wait for approvals. The downtime doubles.

title: The Automation Proposal
prompt: You've identified a manual process that takes 10 hours a week. Automating it would take 3 weeks of effort.

leftChoice.label: Build the automation
leftChoice.outcomeText: The automation saves 40 hours a month going forward. Leadership is impressed by the initiative.

rightChoice.label: Keep doing it manually
rightChoice.outcomeText: The manual work continues to grind you down. The opportunity cost adds up.

title: The Compliance Audit
prompt: An external compliance audit is scheduled for next month. Your documentation is 60% complete.

leftChoice.label: Scramble to complete everything
leftChoice.outcomeText: You pass the audit. The team is exhausted but the company avoids a compliance penalty.

rightChoice.label: Be transparent about the gaps
rightChoice.outcomeText: The auditors flag several gaps. You get a 90-day remediation plan. Leadership is disappointed.

title: The Capacity Planning
prompt: Usage is growing 20% month-over-month. You need to plan for scale. Over-provisioning wastes money; under-provisioning causes outages.

leftChoice.label: Over-provision for safety
leftChoice.outcomeText: No outages. Finance questions the unused capacity spend.

rightChoice.label: Provision tightly to the forecast
rightChoice.outcomeText: Growth spikes beyond forecast. You scramble through two near-outages before catching up.

title: The Ops Ticket Backlog
prompt: Your team's ticket backlog has grown to 200+ items. Leadership wants it cleared in 2 weeks.

leftChoice.label: Triage and tackle the critical ones
leftChoice.outcomeText: You clear the high-priority items and close 80 tickets. Leadership is satisfied.

rightChoice.label: Close stale tickets to hit the number
rightChoice.outcomeText: The backlog looks smaller. Three 'closed' tickets get reopened by angry users the next day.

title: The Ops Playbook
prompt: You've been asked to create a standard operating procedures playbook for your team. It's not glamorous but it's needed.

leftChoice.label: Build a thorough playbook
leftChoice.outcomeText: The playbook becomes the team's bible. Onboarding new hires takes half the time.

rightChoice.label: Do a quick skeleton and move on
rightChoice.outcomeText: The skeleton exists but no one uses it. The same questions keep getting asked.

title: The Cost Optimization
prompt: You've found $50K in annual savings by renegotiating three vendor contracts. It requires 2 months of work.

leftChoice.label: Pursue the savings
leftChoice.outcomeText: The savings are realized. Finance gives you a shout-out in the all-hands.

rightChoice.label: Focus on other priorities
rightChoice.outcomeText: The contracts auto-renew at the higher rate. The savings opportunity passes.

title: The New Tool Rollout
prompt: You're rolling out a new ops tool to 50 users. Some teams are resistant to change.

leftChoice.label: Mandate adoption with training
leftChoice.outcomeText: Adoption is bumpy but complete. Six months later everyone agrees it was the right call.

rightChoice.label: Make it optional and let it spread
rightChoice.outcomeText: Half the teams adopt it. The other half keep using the old tool. Fragmentation ensues.

title: The Ops Metrics Review
prompt: Your quarterly ops metrics show uptime is 99.5% — just below the 99.9% target. Leadership wants an explanation.

leftChoice.label: Present root cause and remediation plan
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership appreciates the transparency and clear action plan. Trust is maintained.

rightChoice.label: Reframe the metric as 'industry standard'
rightChoice.outcomeText: Leadership sees through the spin. You're asked to present a real plan next week.

title: The Disaster Recovery Test
prompt: The annual DR test is due. Running it properly requires a 4-hour maintenance window that will affect users.

leftChoice.label: Run the full DR test
leftChoice.outcomeText: The DR test reveals two gaps you fix immediately. Six months later a real incident is handled smoothly.

rightChoice.label: Run a partial test to avoid downtime
rightChoice.outcomeText: The partial test passes. The untested gaps surface during a real incident three months later.

title: The Ops Hire
prompt: You need to hire an ops analyst. One candidate is technically strong but has poor communication skills. The other is a great communicator but needs technical training.

leftChoice.label: Hire the technical candidate
leftChoice.outcomeText: Great at the work, terrible in stakeholder meetings. You spend months coaching communication.

rightChoice.label: Hire the communicator
rightChoice.outcomeText: Stakeholders love them. You invest in technical training. They become a well-rounded ops analyst.

title: The Change Management
prompt: A major process change is rolling out next week. The team hasn't been properly briefed.

leftChoice.label: Delay and run proper change comms
leftChoice.outcomeText: The delay is worth it. The rollout goes smoothly because everyone knows what to expect.

rightChoice.label: Launch on schedule and deal with questions
rightChoice.outcomeText: The launch is chaotic. Your inbox floods with confused questions for a week.

title: The Ops Dashboard
prompt: Leadership wants a real-time ops dashboard. Building it properly takes 3 weeks. A basic version takes 2 days.

leftChoice.label: Build the proper dashboard
leftChoice.outcomeText: The dashboard becomes the go-to for all ops visibility. Leadership references it daily.

rightChoice.label: Ship the basic version fast
rightChoice.outcomeText: The basic version is used briefly, then abandoned when its limitations become apparent.

title: The Ops Offboarding
prompt: A key ops team member is leaving in 2 weeks. Their knowledge transfer plan is thin.

leftChoice.label: Dedicate time to a proper handover
leftChoice.outcomeText: The handover is thorough. The transition is smooth. The team barely misses a beat.

rightChoice.label: Let them handle their own handover
rightChoice.outcomeText: Critical knowledge walks out the door. The next three months are painful.

title: The Escalation Matrix
prompt: There's no clear escalation path for ops incidents. Everyone escalates to you by default.

leftChoice.label: Build a proper escalation matrix
leftChoice.outcomeText: The matrix is adopted. Your inbox quiets down significantly. The team handles more independently.

rightChoice.label: Keep being the default escalation point
rightChoice.outcomeText: You're always available and always exhausted. The team never builds escalation judgment.

title: The Ops Budget
prompt: You're asked to cut 15% from the ops budget. You can cut tools, headcount, or vendor contracts.

leftChoice.label: Cut tools and renegotiate contracts
leftChoice.outcomeText: You find the savings without touching headcount. The team respects the decision.

rightChoice.label: Reduce headcount
rightChoice.outcomeText: Finance is happy. Team morale craters. The remaining team is stretched dangerously thin.

title: The Process Audit
prompt: You've been asked to audit a process owned by another team. You find significant inefficiencies.

leftChoice.label: Report findings diplomatically
leftChoice.outcomeText: The other team is initially defensive but ultimately grateful. The process improves.

rightChoice.label: Soften the findings to avoid conflict
rightChoice.outcomeText: The report is well-received but nothing changes. The inefficiencies persist.

title: The On-Call Rotation
prompt: Your team's on-call rotation is burning people out. You can hire a contractor to cover nights or restructure the rotation.

leftChoice.label: Hire a contractor for nights
leftChoice.outcomeText: The team gets proper rest. Incident response quality improves. Finance questions the cost.

rightChoice.label: Restructure the rotation
rightChoice.outcomeText: The restructure helps somewhat. People are still tired but less resentful.

title: The Ops Retrospective
prompt: A major incident last month revealed systemic issues. The post-mortem identified 12 action items.

leftChoice.label: Commit to all 12 action items
leftChoice.outcomeText: All 12 items are completed. The system is significantly more resilient. The team is drained.

rightChoice.label: Prioritize the top 5
rightChoice.outcomeText: The critical gaps are fixed. The remaining 7 items sit in the backlog, mostly forgotten.

title: The Ops Intern
prompt: You have a summer intern who's eager but inexperienced. You can give them real work or safe, low-stakes tasks.

leftChoice.label: Give them real, meaningful work
leftChoice.outcomeText: The intern rises to the challenge and delivers. They return full-time after graduation.

rightChoice.label: Keep them on safe, low-stakes tasks
rightChoice.outcomeText: The intern is bored and underutilized. They leave with a lukewarm impression of the team.

title: The Ops Tooling Debt
prompt: Your team is running on a patchwork of legacy tools. Modernizing would take 6 months but would pay off long-term.

leftChoice.label: Propose a modernization roadmap
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership approves. The migration is painful but the new stack is dramatically more efficient.

rightChoice.label: Keep patching the legacy tools
rightChoice.outcomeText: The patches keep things running. The debt compounds. Every incident takes twice as long to resolve.

title: The Ops All-Hands
prompt: You've been asked to present the ops team's quarterly results at the company all-hands.

leftChoice.label: Present the full picture — wins and misses
leftChoice.outcomeText: The transparency earns respect. Leadership appreciates the honest assessment.

rightChoice.label: Highlight only the wins
rightChoice.outcomeText: The presentation is polished. Someone in the audience asks about the SLA miss. Awkward.

title: The Ops Outsourcing
prompt: Leadership is considering outsourcing part of your ops function to reduce costs. You're asked for your recommendation.

leftChoice.label: Recommend selective outsourcing
leftChoice.outcomeText: The selective approach saves money while keeping critical functions in-house. A balanced outcome.

rightChoice.label: Recommend keeping everything in-house
rightChoice.outcomeText: Leadership overrules you and outsources anyway. Your recommendation is noted but ignored.

title: The Cross-Functional Dependency
prompt: A critical ops project is blocked by the engineering team for 3 weeks. You can escalate or find a workaround.

leftChoice.label: Escalate to leadership
leftChoice.outcomeText: The escalation unblocks the project. Engineering is annoyed. The project moves forward.

rightChoice.label: Build a workaround
rightChoice.outcomeText: The workaround works but adds complexity. The root dependency is never resolved.

title: The Ops Knowledge Base
prompt: Your team's knowledge base is outdated and scattered. Building a proper one takes significant effort.

leftChoice.label: Invest in a proper knowledge base
leftChoice.outcomeText: The knowledge base transforms onboarding and reduces repeat questions dramatically.

rightChoice.label: Keep using the scattered docs
rightChoice.outcomeText: The same questions get answered over and over. New hires struggle to find information.

title: The Ops Certification
prompt: A relevant ops certification would boost your credibility and the team's capabilities. It requires 3 months of study.

leftChoice.label: Pursue the certification
leftChoice.outcomeText: You pass. The certification opens doors and gives you more credibility in cross-functional discussions.

rightChoice.label: Skip it — too much time
rightChoice.outcomeText: You stay focused on day-to-day work. The certification opportunity passes.

title: The Ops Standup
prompt: Your daily ops standup has ballooned to 45 minutes. The team is frustrated but it's the only time everyone syncs.

leftChoice.label: Restructure to a 15-minute standup
leftChoice.outcomeText: The shorter standup forces focus. The team is happier and more productive.

rightChoice.label: Keep the long standup for visibility
rightChoice.outcomeText: Everyone stays informed but resents the daily time sink. Attendance starts to drop.

title: The Ops Scope Creep
prompt: Other teams keep sending ops requests that are outside your team's scope. Saying no creates friction.

leftChoice.label: Define and enforce scope boundaries
leftChoice.outcomeText: Some teams are annoyed initially. Your team's focus improves dramatically.

rightChoice.label: Keep absorbing the extra work
rightChoice.outcomeText: You're seen as helpful but your team is overwhelmed. Core ops work starts to suffer.

title: The Ops Metrics Redesign
prompt: Your current ops metrics don't reflect actual business impact. Redesigning them requires stakeholder alignment.

leftChoice.label: Lead a metrics redesign initiative
leftChoice.outcomeText: The new metrics tell a much clearer story. Leadership finally understands the ops team's value.

rightChoice.label: Keep the existing metrics
rightChoice.outcomeText: The ops team continues to be undervalued because the metrics don't capture the real impact.

title: The Ops Vendor Failure
prompt: A critical vendor just went offline with no ETA. You have a backup vendor but switching takes 4 hours.

leftChoice.label: Switch to the backup immediately
leftChoice.outcomeText: The 4-hour switch is stressful but the service is restored. Stakeholders appreciate the quick action.

rightChoice.label: Wait for the primary vendor to recover
rightChoice.outcomeText: The vendor takes 8 hours to recover. The extended downtime frustrates stakeholders.

title: The Ops Headcount Request
prompt: Your team is understaffed. You've built a business case for 2 new hires. Leadership is skeptical.

leftChoice.label: Present the data-driven case
leftChoice.outcomeText: The business case is compelling. You get 1 of the 2 requested hires. Better than nothing.

rightChoice.label: Accept the status quo
rightChoice.outcomeText: The team continues to be stretched. Burnout becomes a real risk.

title: The Ops War Room
prompt: A major product launch is tomorrow. You've been asked to run the ops war room for 12 hours.

leftChoice.label: Run the war room yourself
leftChoice.outcomeText: The launch goes smoothly. Your calm coordination is praised by the entire product team.

rightChoice.label: Delegate to a senior team member
rightChoice.outcomeText: The team member handles it well. You miss an opportunity to shine but develop your team.

title: The Ops Feedback Loop
prompt: Your team has no formal feedback mechanism from internal customers. Issues are reported ad hoc.

leftChoice.label: Build a structured feedback process
leftChoice.outcomeText: The feedback reveals three major pain points you weren't aware of. Fixing them dramatically improves satisfaction.

rightChoice.label: Keep the ad hoc approach
rightChoice.outcomeText: Issues continue to surface reactively. The ops team is always firefighting.

title: The Ops Consolidation
prompt: Two redundant ops processes can be merged into one, saving 20% of your team's time. The merge requires a 2-month project.

leftChoice.label: Merge the processes
leftChoice.outcomeText: The merge is complete. The time savings are real and immediately felt by the team.

rightChoice.label: Keep both processes running
rightChoice.outcomeText: The redundancy continues. The inefficiency compounds over time.

title: The Ops Mentorship
prompt: A junior ops analyst asks you to be their mentor. It's rewarding but takes 2 hours a week.

leftChoice.label: Accept the mentorship
leftChoice.outcomeText: The junior analyst grows quickly. They credit you publicly. Your reputation as a leader grows.

rightChoice.label: Decline — too busy
rightChoice.outcomeText: The junior analyst finds another mentor. You miss an opportunity to build your leadership reputation.

title: The Ops Risk Register
prompt: You've identified 8 operational risks but haven't formally documented them. Leadership doesn't know they exist.

leftChoice.label: Build and present a risk register
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership is alarmed but grateful. Two risks are immediately mitigated with additional resources.

rightChoice.label: Keep managing risks informally
rightChoice.outcomeText: One of the undocumented risks materializes. Leadership asks why they weren't informed.

title: The Ops Shift Handover
prompt: The night shift left incomplete handover notes. The morning shift is confused and a critical task was missed.

leftChoice.label: Fix the immediate issue and address the root cause
leftChoice.outcomeText: You fix the missed task and implement a handover checklist. The problem doesn't recur.

rightChoice.label: Fix the immediate issue only
rightChoice.outcomeText: The immediate issue is resolved. The same handover problem happens again two weeks later.

title: The Ops Benchmark
prompt: Industry benchmarks show your ops team is 30% less efficient than peers. Leadership wants a plan.

leftChoice.label: Present an honest improvement plan
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership appreciates the candor. The improvement plan gets funded.

rightChoice.label: Challenge the benchmark methodology
rightChoice.outcomeText: Leadership sees through the deflection. The benchmark stands. You look defensive.

title: The Ops Roadmap
prompt: You've been asked to present a 12-month ops roadmap. You can be ambitious or conservative.

leftChoice.label: Present an ambitious roadmap
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership is excited. You deliver 70% of it. The 30% miss is noticed but the ambition is respected.

rightChoice.label: Present a conservative roadmap
rightChoice.outcomeText: You deliver 100% of it. Leadership wonders why you didn't aim higher.

title: The Ops Peer Review
prompt: A peer's ops process is inefficient and causing downstream problems for your team. They're defensive about it.

leftChoice.label: Raise it directly with the peer
leftChoice.outcomeText: The conversation is uncomfortable but productive. The process improves.

rightChoice.label: Work around their process
rightChoice.outcomeText: You absorb the inefficiency. The root cause remains and the workaround adds complexity.

title: The Ops Continuity Plan
prompt: Your team has no business continuity plan. Building one takes time but a crisis without one could be catastrophic.

leftChoice.label: Build the continuity plan
leftChoice.outcomeText: Six months later a major disruption hits. Your team responds smoothly because the plan exists.

rightChoice.label: Deprioritize — it's unlikely to be needed
rightChoice.outcomeText: A disruption hits. The response is chaotic. Leadership asks why there was no plan.

title: The Ops Efficiency Drive
prompt: Leadership wants a 10% efficiency improvement this quarter. You can achieve it by cutting corners or by genuine process improvement.

leftChoice.label: Genuine process improvement
leftChoice.outcomeText: The improvements are real and sustainable. The team is proud of the work.

rightChoice.label: Cut corners to hit the number
rightChoice.outcomeText: The number is hit. Quality issues surface the following quarter. The shortcuts cost more to fix.

title: The Ops Presentation
prompt: You're presenting the ops strategy to the executive team for the first time. You can go deep on detail or keep it high-level.

leftChoice.label: Keep it high-level and strategic
leftChoice.outcomeText: Executives appreciate the clarity. They ask smart questions. You're invited back for a deeper dive.

rightChoice.label: Go deep on operational detail
rightChoice.outcomeText: Eyes glaze over. The executives lose interest halfway through. The strategy doesn't land.

title: The Ops Supplier Diversity
prompt: Procurement is pushing for supplier diversity. Switching some vendors meets the goal but requires re-evaluation work.

leftChoice.label: Embrace supplier diversity
leftChoice.outcomeText: The new suppliers perform well. The company meets its diversity goals. Your initiative is recognized.

rightChoice.label: Stick with existing vendors
rightChoice.outcomeText: Procurement flags your team for non-compliance. You're asked to revisit the decision.

title: The Ops Escalation
prompt: A recurring issue keeps getting escalated to you even though it's outside your remit. The actual owner isn't fixing it.

leftChoice.label: Fix it yourself and document the gap
leftChoice.outcomeText: The issue is resolved. You document the ownership gap and escalate it formally. Progress.

rightChoice.label: Redirect every escalation to the right owner
rightChoice.outcomeText: You hold the line on ownership. The issue festers because the real owner still doesn't act.

title: The Ops Year-End Review
prompt: It's performance review time. Your team delivered strong results but the work is invisible to most of the company.

leftChoice.label: Proactively share the team's impact
leftChoice.outcomeText: Leadership finally understands what ops does. Budget and headcount requests are approved.

rightChoice.label: Let the work speak for itself
rightChoice.outcomeText: The work is invisible. The ops team is undervalued again. Budget requests are denied.
